articles.title: Week 1: Manager Quotes
articles.meta: Tue 4th August 2026 | Manager Reactions | By Martin Fallon
articles.body:
We’re back! With almost every NWCFL team in League action across this past weekend, there was plenty of scope to speak to club managers for their opinions on what their teams produced on the pitch.

PREMIER DIVISION

Table-toppers Burscough couldn't have asked for a much better start to the new season, after blowing away last season's play-off hopefuls Prestwich Heys 4-1 on home soil. After the full time whistle, new gaffer Phil Stafford said:

Prestwich are a very good side; we knew that going in. They've recruited well and came very close to the play-offs last season. I don't think today was a 4-1 game - I think they gambled, and we've run away with it late on, but I thought our substitutions were outstanding, and our squad was brilliant today.

Another side that arguably upset the odds by taking maximum points from a 2025/26 promotion contender were last season's First Division North winners Nelson. Arron Ripley's side began this new campaign by beating Atherton LR 2-1 away from home, with the gaffer saying afterwards:

We managed a huge three points away from home on Saturday. To do so at the start of the new Prem season against a top opposition in Atherton LR is testament to the lads – they were unbelievable out there and executed the game plan brilliantly.

FIRST DIVISION NORTH

NWCFL new boys Halewood Apollo have wasted no time stamping their presence into the First Division North. They emerged victorious from a 3-1 affair away at Garstang, following which their 3-in-1 owner, chairman and manager Joseph Stocks said:

It was fantastic to start our first ever game in NWCFL away to Garstang. The lads put in a brilliant performance, and we were buzzing to come away with our first win. Hopefully there are many more to come!

Perhaps the game of the weekend came from the Hamdmark Engineering Stadium, where hosts Holker Old Boys edged maximum points away from another new arrival to the division, AFC Knowsley. After a 4-3 goal-fest, joint manager Kevin Watkin called the game:

A fantastic season opener for the fans, packed with goals! The game was very bitty in the first half – there was not a lot of football played, if I'm honest - it was much more of a battle. In the second half, I think we played the better football and got what we deserved in the end, after making mistakes that led to two of the goals that we conceded.

FIRST DIVISION SOUTH

After topping the opening table following their 6-0 win over Telford Town, the New Mills manager Nathan Neequaye had this to say...

"It’s always good to get the first game for a new squad out of the way and we hit the ground running. We were aggressive and on the front foot all through the game. We were defensively solid and every time we went forward, we looked threatening.

"What pleased us the most was how ruthless we was and the work rate of all the players. We told the lads before the game to go out and show the fans and everyone what your capable of, and they certainly did that.

"This team will always give 100% and now focus moves onto Tuesday at Stafford Town which will be a tough test against a decent team."

AFC Bridgnorth are one of the new clubs after a lateral movement in the summer from the Midland League. They ran out 3-1 winners at home to Foley Meir with Manager Jack Griffiths on a high after the win...

"It was a real tough test today in our first NWCL match. I thought my lads were brilliant the first half and had a real good go at Foley Meir. We had three good chances before scoring on the stroke of half time to give us a deserved lead.

"The second half we started slow and Foley got back into it with a 25 yard strike. I changed a few things brought on Charlie Clarke who changed the game for us, and two quick fire goals from Suar eventually killed the game off.

"I thought we controlled large parts of the game, and am really pleased with the three points to start the new season".

Also with a good start was Wolverhampton Casuals who travelled to newcomers Crewe. They returned south with three points after a 3-0 win, with Manager Dean Gill a relieved man after the game saying...

"I had travelled to Crewe to watch them in one of their preseason games and believe we had the hardest fixture of the day yesterday in our division. A lot of credit to Crewe who have great facilities, a friendly and helpful staff/committee and a side who I believe will have a great season.

"I’m glad to get out of there with all three points. We have lots of work still to do but I won’t complain when the mentality that the lads showed was so positive.”

It was also another good day for another newcomer in Brereton Social, who won 2-0 on the road at Market Drayton Town. Manager Matthew Ainger said afterwards...

"It was great to get off the mark with our first win, especially with it being away from home. It could possibly have been by a bigger margin if we’d been a little more ruthless, but overall it was a fantastic performance from the lads.

"It was a great day for the football club, our volunteers, sponsors, supporters and, most importantly, the players, who have all earned the right to be at this level and proved that with the performance against Market Drayton. Our togetherness will be our strength this season, but it’s important we enjoy the win and then move our focus onto Tuesday away at Alsager Town.

"Every game is a test in this league, and we’ll be ready again for the next one."

And finally newcomers Dawley Town staged a late, late comeback to rescue a point in a 2-2 draw at Alsager Town. Manager Tom White said...

"It was fantastic day for Dawley Town, playing our first game at step 6 at Alsager. Both teams gave everything throughout and it was an entertaining game that had everything.

"Both teams had chances throughout the first half but no one could break the deadlock. Alsager scored early in the second half and we decided to go for the game and stick our centre back up top, however this led to us being 2-0 down in the 84th minute.

"But in true typical Dawley style we never give up and ended up grabbing two goals in the space of seven minutes and could have nicked it at the end.

"A great turnaround and our first points in the board, let’s enjoy the journey and give it our all every week. Thank you to Alsager and all the best for the season."

articles.title: Introducing the new member clubs: AFC Bridgnorth
articles.meta: Wed 5th August 2026 | AFC Bridgnorth | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
With the 2026/27 NWCFL campaign nearly underway, now is the perfect time to introduce the new member clubs to their respective divisions.

Or perhaps better – to let the new member clubs introduce themselves.

Earlier this week, I spoke to Steve Groome – secretary at AFC Bridgnorth, who will take their place in the NWCFL First Division South this season following a lateral move from the Midland League after the end of the 2025/26 season.

For the uninitiated, AFC Bridgnorth are actually a phoenix club. The current iteration of the club was founded in 2013, as a direct successor to Bridgnorth Town Football Club, who folded due to financial difficulties earlier in the same year.

Bridgnorth Town, and by extension, AFC Bridgnorth, has roots that go back before the turn of the 20th century. A Bridgnorth Town FC existed in 1899, in the Shropshire & District League, but records of their existence into the early 1900’s are hard to come by.

Another Bridgnorth Town FC sprang up for a single season in 1938, in the Worcestershire Combination (now called the Midland Football Combination), before being forced to fold upon the start of World War II.

Town were reformed after the war, and they made their triumphant return to the newly named Midland Football Combination in the 1968/69 season. This league pyramid would be their home for the next 15 straight seasons, during which time they finished as runners-up twice; in 1977 and 1981, and as champions twice; in 1980 and 1983. The latter of these title wins would be their last season in the Midland Combination.

They earned promotion to the Midland Division of the Southern League pyramid ahead of the 1983/84 campaign, finishing 12th in their first season. They bettered this finish in 1985/86, when they sprang up to 8th in the table.

Across 13 seasons at this level, their highest finish came in the 1994/95 season, when they came 5th in the standings, only five points behind runners-up Ilkeston Town, but a full 19 points behind runaway champions Newport AFC.

The very next season was one to forget, as Bridgnorth Town finished bottom of the pile in the Midland Division, and were relegated from the Southern League as a result. With that, they took their place in the Midland Football Alliance, where they would spend most of the rest of lifespan before folding in the 2010’s.

Save for a season back to the Midland Combination Premier Division in 2005/06 after relegation, and two further years in the West Midlands (Regional) League following a lateral move before promotion, they were a part of the Midland Alliance League furniture until a seventh placed finish in what would be their swansong campaign in 2012/13.

It was at this time that AFC Bridgnorth, under their current name, were founded to replace their predecessors, and they had to start from the bottom as a result. Beginning life in the West Midlands (Regional) League Division One, they won the league at their first attempt in 2014.

They would spend the next five seasons in the Premier Division, finishing as runners-up in both of their first two seasons, including finishing just a point behind 2015/16 champions and current NWCFL members Shawbury United.

They fell into mid-table in the three years preceding the COVID-19 outbreak, finishing as low as 18th in 2017/18. Their last two seasons in the West Midlands (Regional) Division were curtailed by the pandemic, and they were laterally moved to Division One of the Midland League when their old home league lost its Step Six divisional status going into 2021/22.

In four seasons of Midland League football, AFC Bridgnorth’s best finish actually came in their most recent season, when they came in a respectable 10th place in Division One following a mid-season dip in form that saw them fall out of play-off contention.

Still, a divisional move would be on the cards, as they were laterally moved to the NWCFL First Division South ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.

----------

1. How would you describe AFC Bridgnorth to someone who had never heard of the club?

a. AFC Bridgnorth is a friendly club, run by volunteers who just enjoy football at grassroots level. The club is all inclusive and has a growing junior section with many girls’ and boys’ sides included.

The club is situated in a housing estate close to the edge of Bridgnorth, and it is used as a focal point for many community activities.

2. What does the club mean to the area and community that you represent?

a. AFC Bridgnorth is an outlet for many in the local community. The club is used by several social groups during the week, and the junior section make use of the facilities on the weekend.

The club also runs a successful Sunday side which enables more local players to be able to enjoy football. On a Saturday afternoon, there is a small hardcore of locals that support the first team home and away!

3. Tell me about the manager you work with?

a. Jack Griffiths came to Bridgnorth as our U18’s manager in the 2023/24 season, and he was very successful.

He returned as our first team manager midway through the 2024/25 season, and he brought in a new crop of players, most of whom have been vital to helping us reach our goals.

4. Tell me a bit about last season - your last one in the Midland League?

a. Last season was a mixed bag. AFC Bridgnorth started very well and we were looking like play-off candidates. Then several players were swayed away for finances that we unfortunately couldn’t match.

This led to a mixed period where we drew too many matches and ended up in mid-table. The season did finish on a high though, as the club won the Shropshire County Cup, which was certainly something to celebrate!

5. How have you adjusted to the news of your lateral move to the NWCFL?

a. Initially, there was a worry that the travel would be a major problem, but since the league allocations were announced, it seems we might be travelling even less than we did last season.

It will be nice to see several Shropshire derbies back in the fixture schedule, too!

6. How well have you been getting along with your pre-season prep? New signings, friendlies, etc?

a. As a club, we have made several new signings in a push to increase the depth of squad coming out of last season. Our pre-season fixtures have gone very well – we’ve only had one defeat during the build-up to 2026/27.

7. What are your ambitions for the upcoming 2026/27 season in the NWCFL?

a. In our first season, AFC Bridgnorth will be looking to improve on the mid-table finish we managed last season in the Midland League.

If we can keep the squad fit and happy, I would hope that we can be pushing for one of the play-off places this season.

----------

Since this conversation, AFC Bridgnorth have gotten off to perhaps the best start they could've asked for. In their league debut, they dismissed 2025/26 mid-table side Foley Meir 3-1 on home soil.

We wish everyone at AFC Bridgnorth all the best for the 2026/27 season!

articles.title: Five Things We Learned 2026/27: Week 1
articles.meta: Thu 6th August 2026 | Five Things | By Jay Cooper
articles.body:
We’re back! After a year off last season, this article series is returning, and will release weekly on a Thursday.

With the first league matches of the season having been played last weekend, let’s run through the best and worst of what the last seven days have had to offer.

1. Goals galore for Burscough

Phil Stafford’s arrival from AFC Liverpool has been the headline story coming out of Burscough over the course of the summer, and it seems as though the board’s decision to appoint the new gaffer is paying dividends.

They began the season with a home game against last season’s play-off near-misses Prestwich Heys, and took them apart, winning 4-1. On Tuesday evening, they went on the road to face FC St Helens in a greater Liverpool derby, and came out on top in a seven-goal thriller, winning 5-2 to top the table.

2. Cammell Laird 1907 hitting and being hit for six

Away from the Premier Division, if you want goals, it seems as though you can find them pretty easily at the OWS Engineering Ltd Stadium.

Cammell Laird 1907, who were laterally moved to the North from the South ahead of the new season, lost their opening game in a five-goal affair, but won their second in a seven-goal outing. You can tell the season is still very new when the same team have the joint-second most goals scored and conceded in the league.

3. False start for the Chevrons

Steeton will want to forget the last seven days of football. The team from the Marley Stadium have had the toughest of starts in their opening two matches of the First Division North, firstly going down 5-0 away from home to first-week table-toppers Daisy Hill.

Hoping for redemption on home soil against Holker Old Bys. They were again beaten and unable to score against their opponents in a 2-0 defeat, leaving them bottom of the table with a -7 goal difference. The only way is up, at least.

4. Welcome to the NWCFL, Halewood Apollo

The First Division North’s newest arrivals, Halewood Apollo, did not exist 13 years ago. And yet, here they are, taking Step Six of the non-league pyramid by storm in their first two games of the season.

Joseph Stocks’ men won 3-1 on the opening day away at reprieved Garstang, before making it two from two, again away from home, defeating laterally moved Ashville 2-1 on Tuesday. Message sent!

5. Welcome to the NWCFL, AFC Bridgnorth

It would seem that Halewood Apollo are not the only ones! AFC Bridgnorth have started their maiden NWCFL campaign with two wins on the trot, both of which were attained in pretty comprehensive fashion.

They began the season with a 3-1 victory over Foley Meir, who finished mid-table last season in the First Division South. On Wednesday, they followed that up with a 4-0 dismantling of fellow new arrivals Bilston Town away from home, to go joint top of the division alongside Eccleshall and Stafford Town.

articles.title: Week 2: Preview
articles.meta: Fri 7th August 2026 | Match Previews | By Ben Wilkinson
articles.body:
There's no rest for the wicked as the football season is in full flow. Taking the headlines for our Premier Division clubs this weekend is the Emirates FA Cup; as clubs up and down the country dream of a life-changing cup run and the most unlikeliest of Wembley appearances - just 14 rounds away!

The Edward Case Cup also gets off to a start with the Preliminary Round, featuring the newly-promoted clubs and those who finished towards the bottom of last season's standings. Rounding out the weekend is a handful of league games for those who received byes in the ECC.

Saturday 8 August – Emirates FA Cup Extra Preliminary Round

Abbey Hey v Ossett UnitedAbbey Hey come into this tie on the back of a bruising 6-2 midweek defeat at Chadderton, having earlier drawn 2-2 with Barnoldswick Town on the opening day of the Premier Division season. Ossett United, of the Northern Premier League, will come into this tie as favourites but Abbey Hey will fancy their chances if they can tighten up their back line. Ossett are no strangers to NWCFL opposition since their formation in 2018, most recently going 1-0 down at Atherton LR at this stage of the FA Cup last term.

Barnoldswick Town v Atherton CollieriesBarnoldswick have opened their Premier Division campaign with two draws, sharing the points in a 1-1 at Prestwich Heys following on from the opening day draw with Abbey Hey. Atherton Collieries, former NWCFL members but now plying their trade in the Northern Premier League, arrive as higher‑level opposition and will look to impose their quality, but Barnoldswick’s stubborn start suggests this could be a tight cup tie.

Burscough v Droylsden

Burscough have started the Premier Division season in style, beating Prestwich Heys 4-1 and then winning 5-2 away at FC St Helens, marking them out as the early pacesetters and the only side to have won 2 from 2. Droylsden also have a 100% record, but only from one game after their midweek clash against South Liverpool was abandoned. The Linnets harbour high hopes for this campaign following a productive close-season and a good cup run would help breed further confidence.

Chadderton v Witton AlbionChadderton have carried last season’s free-scoring nature into this campaign, the 6-2 win at home to Abbey Hey following a 1-1 at Charnock Richard. Witton Albion, another Northern Premier League club with history in the Counties, are the higher-ranked side here but Chadderton’s home advantage, momentum and goalscoring form make this one ripe for a ‘cupset’.

Clitheroe v AFC LiverpoolClitheroe, another NPL Division One West outfit, host AFC Liverpool, who have endured a tough start to the season with defeats to Droylsden and Euxton Villa. The Non-League Reds will hope the cup offers a reset, but Clitheroe will pose a very tough test at their Shawbridge ground and have had recent cup competition exploits of their own.

Euxton Villa v Atherton LRThis is an all-Premier Division tie between two sides who have had a mixed start to the campaign, winning one and losing one each. The H2H between the pair is also finely poised - LR have won 5 of the 9 previous meetings, the other four going the way of Villa, though Dave Jones’ side did win both league games last term, including a thumping 5-0 win away at Euxton.

Handsworth v Prestwich HeysHandsworth, from the Northern Counties East League, welcome Prestwich Heys, who have had a mixed Premier Division start; heavy defeat at Burscough followed by a 1-1 draw with Barnoldswick Town. Prestwich will hope to continue that improvement into the cup, while Handsworth will look to use home advantage to bridge the gap to their NWCFL visitors.

Keighley Town v Longridge TownKeighley Town (the new name for ex-NWCFL side Eccleshill United) step into the FA Cup against Longridge Town, who lost 3-0 at new boys Trafford in the Premier Division last weekend.

Litherland REMYCA v Charnock Richard Litherland REMYCA have taken one point from two Premier Division games; a 1-1 draw with Ramsbottom United followed by a 2-0 home defeat to Charnock Richard. The cup brings an immediate rematch, and Charnock will be confident of another victory, though REMYCA will be desperate to respond and avoid back‑to‑back home losses to the same opponent.

Nelson v Stockport GeorgiansNelson, promoted as last season’s First Division North champions, have already shown they can compete at Premier Division level with a 2-1 win at Atherton LR before their home game with Longridge was postponed midweek. Stockport Georgians, newly up from the First Division South and now in the Midland League, make their FA Cup debut, and this tie may prove to be a good yardstick for both sides.

North Ferriby v FC St HelensNorth Ferriby, of the Northern Counties East League, host FC St Helens, who have had a rough start in the Premier Division with defeats to FC Isle of Man and a 5-2 thumping at home to Burscough. St Helens will hope the cup offers respite from league struggles, but this may be a daunting away assignment on Humberside.

Ramsbottom United v South Liverpool Ramsbottom United have begun the Premier Division season impressively, drawing at Litherland REMYCA and then beating Trafford 3-0 at home. South Liverpool have drawn with Irlam and seen a game abandoned at Droylsden, so they’re still searching for a first victory of the campaign.

Tadcaster Albion v Glossop North End Tadcaster Albion, from the Northern Premier League, welcome Glossop North End, who have started well in the Premier Division with a 2-0 win over Euxton Villa and a goalless draw against FC Isle of Man. Glossop’s defence will surely be tested by Step 4 opposition, but their early form suggests they won’t be overawed by the trip to Yorkshire.

Saturday 8 August – Edward Case Cup Preliminary Round North

Fulwood Amateurs v Halewood ApolloFulwood Amateurs have taken four points from two First Division North games, drawing at Maine Road and winning away at Squires Gate whilst Halewood Apollo have taken to the NWCFL like a duck to water and have beaten Garstang and Ashville and will be looking to make it three in three and progress to the first round.

Maine Road v AFC BlackpoolAFC Blackpool have suffered back-to-back defeats to open their season whilst hosts Maine Road followed up an opening day draw at home to Fulwood with a narrow reverse against Bacup during the week. Two sides who are perhaps expected to struggle this season - a bit of a cup run could be just what one of them needs to boost confidence.

Steeton v AFC KnowsleySteeton have had an horror start to the season, a 5-0 defeat at Daisy Hill only slightly improved by a 2-0 loss at home to Holker Old Boys, results that leave them at the foot of the table at this very early stage. AFC Knowsley’s life in the NWCFL hasn’t got off to an ideal start either as they are also yet to open their account this season. One of these will taste victory for the first time on Saturday afternoon, and with it safe passage into the next round.

Uppermill v Daisy HillUppermill have taken a point from their first two First Division North games following promotion, drawing at Ashville and losing 3-0 at Ashton Athletic. Daisy Hill, by contrast, have started superbly with big wins over Steeton and AFC Knowsley, scoring freely; this particular tie pits a side still settling into the division against one riding high on early‑season confidence.

Other fixtures:

Saturday 8 August – Edward Case Cup Preliminary Round South

AFC Bridgnorth v Bilston Town

AFC Bridgnorth began their debut First Division South campaign with a 3-1 home win over Foley Meir and then followed it up with a thumping win away at Saturday’s opposition: Bilston Town, another side new to the NWCFL. Football throws up shocks all the time and the weekend’s hosts will be making absolutely no assumptions based on the midweek meeting.

Dawley Town v Brereton Social Dawley Town’s first home game in the Counties takes the form of an outing against fellow freshmen Brereton Social. Dawley’s four goals thus far have only translated into one point, whilst back-to-back 2-0 wins for Brereton have given them a dream start. If they can keep their defence as tight as that, they may well be able to keep the Dawley strike force at bay.

Wednesfield Community v Widnes Town

Wednesfield Community have had a mixed start to life in the First Division South, beating Dawley Town 3-2 at home during the week to get their first points on the board after an opening day reverse. Widnes Town have struggled somewhat in their opening exchanges and are yet to secure their first win in their history.

Other fixtures:

Saturday 8 August – First Division North

Bacup Borough v Ashville

Bacup Borough have started the season superbly, beating Ashton Town 3-0 and then winning 3-2 at Maine Road, putting them among the early pace‑setters in First Division North with a perfect record so far. Ashville have taken one point from their two games, drawing with Uppermill but losing at home to Halewood Apollo, so this trip to an in‑form Bacup side looks a stern early‑season examination.

Cammell Laird 1907 v Squires Gate

Cammell Laird’s first two games have been dramatic - a 4-3 win at Flixton followed by a narrow 3-2 defeat at Thornton Cleveleys puts them at the top end of both the goals scored and against columns. Squires Gate have drawn with Flixton and lost at home to Fulwood Amateurs, so both of these sides are still searching for a bit of consistency; this fixture could hinge on which defence settles quickest.

Maghull v Holker Old Boys

Maghull have had a mixed start, losing at Darwen but beating AFC Blackpool 1-0 at home to get their points tally on the rise. Holker Old Boys, meanwhile, have won both games in high‑scoring fashion against AFC Knowsley and Steeton, so they arrive looking to extend their perfect start and will test Maghull’s defensive organisation.

Other fixtures:

Saturday 8 August – First Division South

Foley Meir v Shawbury UnitedFoley Meir lost 3-1 at AFC Bridgnorth but bounced back with a 3-2 home win over Sandbach United. Shawbury United have drawn at Telford Town and lost narrowly at Stafford Town in their opening duo, so they’ll be keen to find a first win of the season up in ST3, and expect goals galore in this one.

New Mills v Allscott HeathNew Mills have had possibly the most up-and-down start to the season you will ever see; the high of an opening day 6-0 win at home to Telford Town was soon replaced with despair as Stafford Town hit them for five without reply on Tuesday evening. The visitors to Church Lane on Saturday, Allscott Heath, also come into this clash off the back of a heavy defeat as they went down 4-0 to Eccleshall. Both sides therefore come into this one needing a reaction, and the outcome could shape their early‑season confidence.

Sandbach United v Stafford TownThese two familiar foes have both been at the upper end of the First Division South table for the past couple of years without tasting success. The visiting Stafford side have won two from two so far, including a 5-0 drubbing of New Mills during the week.

Other fixtures:

Sunday 9 August – Emirates FA Cup Extra Preliminary Round

Sunday sees two Premier Division clubs travel over the Pennines to face Yorkshire opposition in the FA Cup. Trafford go to Worsborough Bridge Athletic off the back of a hot and cold start to life back in the NWCFL, flying off the mark with a 3-0 win over Longridge before losing by the same scoreline at Ramsbottom United. Trafford may be expected to triumph here, but Worsborough Bridge will be looking to make a good start to their first FA Cup campaign since 2002-03! Their previous history against NWCFL opposition in the FA Vase will be something they want to change too, having lost their last seven outings!

Also on Sunday, Irlam travel east to take on Sheffield-based NCEL side Hallam.
